data.note:
Reflection: concluded Aurora kinase inhibitors, truth microtubule destabilizers (demecolcine/colcemid).

What misled: all 4 wells 0.1-10 uM were saturated multinucleate/polyploid (form_factor z ~-45 to -51, multinucleate_proxy z 14-17, large-nucleus z 14-23, count z ~-11) with flat mitotic index (z -0.4 to -0.9). Atlas NSC voted Eg5 3/4, microscopist voted Aurora twice. PI correctly flagged 0.68 overstated; I then over-weighted the second microscopy read and flat mitotic trend and flipped to Aurora. Neither mitotic class was correct - prolonged microtubule depolymerization at 24h produces the same failed-mitosis/slippage multinucleation, and actin-dominated profile masked tubulin loss.

Literature confirms colcemid as tubulin agent: resistance mutations in tubulin confer colcemid resistance (PMID 17938271, PMID 12883031, PMID 22669706).

Lesson: for saturated polyploid phenotypes, do not choose between Aurora/Eg5 on morphology alone; keep microtubule agents on board and titrate lower to catch early spindle/monopolar arrest.

reflection.text:
Initial Eg5 call (p=0.68) came from NSC 3/4 wells and 8/10 neighbours, but all four wells (0.1-10 uM) showed saturated nuclear shape defects (nuc_form_factor z -45 to -51, nuc_solidity z -36 to -62) and saturated multinucleation that Eg5, Aurora and microtubule agents share. The review correctly flagged overstatement because frac_mitotic_like was flat/negative (z -0.4 to -0.9, rho=-0.95) with no Eg5-specific arrest, and I then overcorrected to Aurora (p=0.55) on the free low-dose describe_phenotype of spread multinucleates.

Truth was demecolcine, a colcemid microtubule destabilizer acting via tubulin (PMID 17938271) where stabilizing tubulin mutations confer colcemid resistance (PMID 12883031). The destabilizer signal was present but dismissed: the 0.1 uM well nearest was Microtubule stabilizers (sim 0.567), 2/10 neighbours were Microtubule stabilizers, and act_tub_ratio z=+17.9 hinted tubulin cytoskeleton change alongside severe nuclear irregularity.

The miss was an acquisition choice plus weighting error: sampling only 0.1, 0.3, 1 and 10 uM left the 0.003-0.03 uM onset unsampled where microtubule loss versus monopolar arrest diverges, and I weighted qualitative microscopist Aurora calls over quantitative atlas and tubulin literature (PMID 22669706), misreading absent mitotics as Aurora-specific slippage when saturated destabilizer slippage looks the same.
what_was_right: Captured severe mitotic-failure phenotype: extreme nuc_form_factor/solidity loss, frac_large_nucleus z +19 to +23, and lower density across doses, correctly keeping mitotic hypotheses and deprioritizing DNA replication at 0.05.
Recognized saturation confound: 0.1-10 uM all multinucleate/polyploid so Eg5 and Aurora could both explain it, and review correctly noted 0.68 overstated Eg5 without strong Eg5-specific arrest.
Flagged absent Eg5-type arrest: frac_mitotic_like flat/negative with rho=-0.95 was real evidence against canonical prolonged monopolar arrest at those doses.
what_was_wrong: Sampled only high saturated doses (0.1, 0.3, 1, 10 uM) and never acquired 0.003-0.03 uM onset wells where destabilizer microtubule depolymerization versus Eg5 monopolar spindles would separate.

Flipped from atlas-driven Eg5 to microscopist-driven Aurora on free low-dose describe_phenotype without a new quantitative discriminator, overweighting qualitative Aurora calls (e4, e14) over NSC votes.
Discarded microtubule hypothesis despite 1/4 wells nearest Microtubule stabilizers, 2/10 k-neighbours as Microtubule stabilizers, and act_tub_ratio z=+17.9 tubulin signal at 0.1 uM.

Misinterpreted negative mitotic_like trend as Aurora-specific cytokinesis failure/slippage, when prolonged demecolcine destabilization at saturated doses also yields slippage to spread multinucleates with low mitotic index.

citations.claim: Beta-tubulin Pro220 substitutions confer resistance to colcemid (demecolcine), supporting a direct tubulin mechanism.
Alpha- and beta-tubulin mutations that stabilize microtubules confer resistance to colcemid and vinblastine, consistent with demecolcine as a microtubule destabilizer.
Systematic beta-tubulin mutagenesis defines dispersed residues that alter microtubule-drug sensitivity, illustrating tubulin as the target hub for these agents.

reflection.next_experiment: Low-nM titration of demecolcine versus Eg5-inhibitor, Aurora-inhibitor, stabilizer and destabilizer controls with alpha-tubulin plus centrosome plus DNA plus phospho-H3 staining and live mitotic timing to test for dose-dependent microtubule loss and mitotic slippage versus monopolar arrest or cytokinesis failure.

## Conclusion 1

**Eg5 inhibitors** (stated probability 0.68); key evidence e8, e2, e6, e7, e4, e9.

Why: NSC 3/4 Eg5 with 8/10 neighbours; all doses share multinucleate polyploid profile; microscopist confirms mitotic failure.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: High-resolution spindle assay: stain treated vs reference-class controls for tubulin plus centrosome marker and phospho-H3 to test for monopolar spindles with mitotic delay versus multilobed polyploid slippage.

## Conclusion 2

**Aurora kinase inhibitors** (stated probability 0.55); key evidence e14, e4, e11, e6, e7, e8.

Why: Requested low-dose imaging done with no new well needed; spread multinucleate dominates, flat mitotic index opposes Eg5, so favor Aurora over atlas.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Spindle/cytokinesis assay with phospho-H3 plus tubulin/centrosome markers versus reference-class controls, plus titration below 0.1 uM to catch early arrest before saturated multinucleation; budget is spent so no new wells here.

## PI review

Verdict: request experiment.

Not approved. 0.68 overstates support for Eg5. Atlas 3/4 Eg5 is the only class-specific evidence and conflicts with the microscopist, who directly favored Aurora and noted overlapping mitotic defects. The four acquired doses (0.1-10 uM) all show saturated multinucleation/polyploidy (frac_multinucleate_proxy z ~14-17), which both Eg5 and Aurora could explain. Crucially, Eg5-type mitotic arrest is not seen: frac_mitotic_like is flat/negative (z -0.4 to -0.9) across doses. No result is both strong and Eg5-specific.

Requested: FREE describe_phenotype on the already-acquired lowest-dose well (dose_index 3, 0.1 uM, replicate 1), specifically scoring rounded mitotic cells/tubulin aster organization versus spread multinucleate interphase cells. This directly tests Eg5-type monopolar mitotic arrest against Aurora-type cytokinesis failure without new budget, and could confound if monopolar mitotics are absent.

## Unblinding

Compound: **demecolcine** (PubChem CID [220401](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/220401))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule destabilizers**.

## Reflection

Initial Eg5 call (p=0.68) came from NSC 3/4 wells and 8/10 neighbours, but all four wells (0.1-10 uM) showed saturated nuclear shape defects (nuc_form_factor z -45 to -51, nuc_solidity z -36 to -62) and saturated multinucleation that Eg5, Aurora and microtubule agents share. The review correctly flagged overstatement because frac_mitotic_like was flat/negative (z -0.4 to -0.9, rho=-0.95) with no Eg5-specific arrest, and I then overcorrected to Aurora (p=0.55) on the free low-dose describe_phenotype of spread multinucleates.

Truth was demecolcine, a colcemid microtubule destabilizer acting via tubulin (PMID 17938271) where stabilizing tubulin mutations confer colcemid resistance (PMID 12883031). The destabilizer signal was present but dismissed: the 0.1 uM well nearest was Microtubule stabilizers (sim 0.567), 2/10 neighbours were Microtubule stabilizers, and act_tub_ratio z=+17.9 hinted tubulin cytoskeleton change alongside severe nuclear irregularity.

The miss was an acquisition choice plus weighting error: sampling only 0.1, 0.3, 1 and 10 uM left the 0.003-0.03 uM onset unsampled where microtubule loss versus monopolar arrest diverges, and I weighted qualitative microscopist Aurora calls over quantitative atlas and tubulin literature (PMID 22669706), misreading absent mitotics as Aurora-specific slippage when saturated destabilizer slippage looks the same.

What was right:
- Captured severe mitotic-failure phenotype: extreme nuc_form_factor/solidity loss, frac_large_nucleus z +19 to +23, and lower density across doses, correctly keeping mitotic hypotheses and deprioritizing DNA replication at 0.05.
- Recognized saturation confound: 0.1-10 uM all multinucleate/polyploid so Eg5 and Aurora could both explain it, and review correctly noted 0.68 overstated Eg5 without strong Eg5-specific arrest.
- Flagged absent Eg5-type arrest: frac_mitotic_like flat/negative with rho=-0.95 was real evidence against canonical prolonged monopolar arrest at those doses.

What was wrong or missed:
- Sampled only high saturated doses (0.1, 0.3, 1, 10 uM) and never acquired 0.003-0.03 uM onset wells where destabilizer microtubule depolymerization versus Eg5 monopolar spindles would separate.
- Flipped from atlas-driven Eg5 to microscopist-driven Aurora on free low-dose describe_phenotype without a new quantitative discriminator, overweighting qualitative Aurora calls (e4, e14) over NSC votes.
- Discarded microtubule hypothesis despite 1/4 wells nearest Microtubule stabilizers, 2/10 k-neighbours as Microtubule stabilizers, and act_tub_ratio z=+17.9 tubulin signal at 0.1 uM.
- Misinterpreted negative mitotic_like trend as Aurora-specific cytokinesis failure/slippage, when prolonged demecolcine destabilization at saturated doses also yields slippage to spread multinucleates with low mitotic index.

Proposed next experiment: Low-nM titration of demecolcine versus Eg5-inhibitor, Aurora-inhibitor, stabilizer and destabilizer controls with alpha-tubulin plus centrosome plus DNA plus phospho-H3 staining and live mitotic timing to test for dose-dependent microtubule loss and mitotic slippage versus monopolar arrest or cytokinesis failure.

## Citations

Citations verified: 3/3

- PMID [17938271](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17938271/): Amino acid substitutions at proline 220 of beta-tubulin confer resistance to paclitaxel and colcemid. *Mol Cancer Ther* (2007) — Beta-tubulin Pro220 substitutions confer resistance to colcemid (demecolcine), supporting a direct tubulin mechanism.
- PMID [12883031](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12883031/): Mutations in alpha- and beta-tubulin that stabilize microtubules and confer resistance to colcemid and vinblastine. *Mol Cancer Ther* (2003) — Alpha- and beta-tubulin mutations that stabilize microtubules confer resistance to colcemid and vinblastine, consistent with demecolcine as a microtubule destabilizer.
- PMID [22669706](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22669706/): Random mutagenesis of β-tubulin defines a set of dispersed mutations that confer paclitaxel resistance. *Pharm Res* (2012) — Systematic beta-tubulin mutagenesis defines dispersed residues that alter microtubule-drug sensitivity, illustrating tubulin as the target hub for these agents.
